fields.v: Kim, J., Kim, M., Kim, Y. J., Pereira, M., Côté, M.-A., Sordoni, A., Yuan, X., & Shi, Z. (2026). ProgramDistill: From Interactive Web Apps to Verifiable Reference-Guided SWE Tasks. arXiv:2609.18805v1 [cs.SE], 16 Sep 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2609.18805v1 [cs.SE]; no venue stated
Academia and industry: KAIST; Microsoft Research Montréal; Microsoft AI

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — ProgramDistill, a benchmark of reference-guided web development built by an automated mine-craft-patch pipeline (1,975 replay-verified behaviors, 4,063 tasks from 26 web applications), used to compare nine frontier models in partial-application reconstruction and three in full-application reconstruction

No SDD approach. Agents compared: one modified R2E-Gym harness (tools execute_bash, file_editor, search, finish, plus browser CLI) with nine models: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.7 Flash, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, Grok 4.6, GPT-5.3 Codex. Harness version: Not stated. Benchmark construction pipeline (mine-craft-patch) uses GPT-5.6 Sol

Not an approach. Task inputs: a working reference application (source hidden), the masked current repository and a generated behavioral problem statement (partial reconstruction), or a minimal executable scaffold and a product-level capability description (full reconstruction); replay-verified behavior traces serve as hidden verifiers; gold patches

N/A (no development flow prescribed). Pipeline: mine (discover and replay-verify behaviors), craft (mask implementations, validate, compose cumulative tasks), patch (agent restores behavior). Agent instruction: explore reference, edit current application, validate against reference, submit; fresh verifier replays traces
None: tasks constructed without human intervention and agents run autonomously
N/A (no SDD approach); full agent runs on repair and reconstruction tasks where the working application acts as the specification
Not classifiable (authors' wording: 'treat running software itself as part of the specification', 'shift from specification consumption to specification discovery')
Existing code base (partial-application reconstruction: restore masked features in a repository) and new project from a minimal scaffold (full-application reconstruction)

26 web applications (18 OSWorld-derived, 8 open-source projects/SaaS clones); 4,063 tasks (2,862 atomic, 1,201 cumulative); evaluation suite ProgramDistill-300 (50 atomic, 250 cumulative, restoration depth 1-8, 269 lineages); full reconstruction: 12 applications, 590 atomic and 413 cumulative behavior tests. Restoration code size grows 9.3x from depth 1 to 8 (absolute LOC not stated in text)
Interactive web applications (e.g. Trello and Jira clones, AWS Console, Baserow, Reactive Resume, Actual Budget, MailHub, StreamView, W&B, banking, insurance, scheduling)
N/A (autonomous agents)

Mean trajectory cost in USD (uncached input, cached input and output tokens x LiteLLM list prices); agent steps; wall-clock time for one representative run (GPT-6 Astra: 300 tasks in ~557 min on four servers, 48.2 min mean per trial); prompt size per step
Binary score (whole task lineage passes replay verification), chain score (partial credit for recovered prefix); full reconstruction: atomic behavior recovery and cumulative binary/chain recovery
None (patches need not match the gold patch; only behavior checked). Retention of unchanged target files and mask stub lines in final patches reported
None

Interaction behaviour: reference/current observation steps, read/search steps, edit/write steps, browser state returns; shortcut attempts (Git history, public source fetches, protected harness probes, direct reference probes); failure categories (not observed, observed not implemented, wrong observable form, wrong state/result)

Automatic: fresh verifier rebuilds the submitted application and replays held-out traces without LLM intervention; cost from token logs and LiteLLM prices; trajectory statistics from logs. Failure analysis of 977 failed atomic behaviors classified with GPT-6 Astra

Criterion: replay verification of behavior traces (binary/chain score); no success threshold stated by the authors, so verdicts for all entries: no criterion stated by the authors. One trial per task per configuration (no repetitions stated). Partial-application reconstruction, ProgramDistill-300, modified R2E-Gym harness, high reasoning effort; mean binary score, mean cost per trajectory: (a) + GPT-6 Astra: 84.3%, $33.99 (depth 1 100%, depth 8 64.0%). (b) + Claude Opus 5: 68.7%, $28.86 (96% -> 32%). (c) + GPT-5.6 Sol: 60.7%, $16.01 (92% -> 32%). (d) + Grok 4.6: 48.3%, $8.83. (e) + Claude Sonnet 5: 47.3%, $13.12. (f) + GPT-5.3 Codex: 45.7%, $5.99. (g) + Gemini 3.7 Flash: 45.3%, $3.89. (h) + Gemini 3.6 Flash: 29.7%, cost in figure only. (i) + Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview: 22.3%, cost in figure only. Full-application reconstruction, 12 apps, one run each, max reasoning effort; atomic recovery / cumulative binary / cumulative chain: (j) + GPT-6 Astra: 58.98 / 49.15 / 64.58%. (k) + Claude Opus 5: 42.03 / 28.81 / 47.42%. (l) + GPT-5.6 Sol: 33.39 / 21.07 / 34.22%. Mean steps per run ~719, 628, 719

Tasks: ProgramDistill-300 (stratified by restoration depth, round-robin across 26 apps) and 12 apps for full reconstruction. Configurations: nine models in the same modified R2E-Gym harness (three in full reconstruction). Constant: harness, tools, instructions, isolation (no Git history, no egress, hidden grading files), step and token limits (partial: 1,000 steps, high effort; full: 10,000 steps, max effort). Baseline: none (gold patch replay used as solvability control). Acceptance: replay of held-out behavior traces in a fresh verifier. Repetitions: not stated (single trial). Human intervention: none

Partial reconstruction: GPT-6 Astra best (84.3%), 15.7 points above Opus 5 at ~18% higher cost per trajectory; middle tier 45.3-48.3%; Gemini 3.7 Flash nearly matches GPT-5.3 Codex at lower cost ($3.89 vs $5.99); performance falls with restoration depth for all models. Full reconstruction: Astra > Opus 5 > Sol on atomic and cumulative recovery, same order as partial. Logic-and-UI masks harder than logic-only (Astra 16.0-point binary gap). Shortcut attempts in 7.2% of trajectories (Grok 4.6 19.0%, Astra 0.3%). No significance tests

Partly: it separated models and gave a controllable difficulty axis; model order consistent across partial and full settings. Repeatability not assessed (single trial, no variance). Limitations stated by the authors: text-only browser observations, self-contained web apps only, construction model (GPT-5.6 Sol) may affect task coverage and quality, dependence on browser and harness infrastructure

Limitations: no screenshot inputs or visual fidelity evaluation; only self-contained web applications (no external services, nondeterministic state, desktop or mobile); construction relies on one model; sensitivity to browser helper and harness not characterised; potential misuse for cloning applications. Gaps: agents' observation and validation effort per behavior falls as depth grows; most full-reconstruction failures are behaviors never observed (59.2%); agents' own validation misses mismatches

Abstract and introduction quote full-reconstruction cumulative success 49.2% / 28.8%; Table 1 gives 49.15 / 28.81. Per-trajectory costs for Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview only in Figure 7(a). Table 1 is garbled in the extracted text; means taken from text. Benchmark not yet public ('working on a public release'); applications pinned to commits (Table 3). No pre-registration. Programming language: web stacks (Django, Angular, React, Next.js); full reconstruction contract in JavaScript (app.js)

Yes (1): binary and chain scores defined; cost per trajectory and steps reported
Yes (1): nine models under the same harness and conditions

Yes (1): conclusions follow from the results, including the weak full-reconstruction results

Yes (1): no evaluated model or harness is by the authors (Microsoft authors; models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI)
fields.why: By the letter of §5 Yes holds: none of the evaluated models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI) nor the base R2E-Gym harness is made by the authors' employers (KAIST, Microsoft). Whether Microsoft's commercial tie to OpenAI (top model GPT-6 Astra; tasks built with GPT-5.6 Sol) counts as dependence is a judgement.
fields.doubt: Os autores são da Microsoft, parceira da OpenAI; o GPT-6 Astra fica em primeiro e as tarefas foram geradas com o GPT-5.6 Sol. Decide se isto conta como dependência (Partly) ou se mantém Yes.
